## Reset memory
```{r setup-packages, include false}
rm(list = ls(all.names = TRUE))
lapply(paste('package:',names(sessionInfo()$otherPkgs),sep=""),detach,character.only=TRUE,unload=TRUE,force=TRUE)
gc()
```

## New way to load required packages
```{r load-packages, include false}
options("install.lock" = FALSE,
        "repos" = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org")) # Replace with your target repo URL
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman") ; library(pacman)
pacman::p_load(
  rio,          # File import
  here,         # File locator
  skimr,        # get overview of data
  tidyverse,    # data management + ggplot2 graphics, 
  gtsummary,    # summary statistics and tests
  rstatix,      # statistics
  nortest,      # Anderson-Darling test for normality
  moments,      # skewness and kurtosis
  corrr,        # correlation analayis for numeric variables
  janitor,      # adding totals and percents to tables
  readr,
  flextable,    # converting tables to HTML
  dplyr,        # For data manipulation
  ggplot2,      # For creating plots
  plotly,
  DescTools,    # For statistical functions like skewness and kurtosis
  car,          # For Levene's test and ANOVA
  vctrs,         # For data type handling
  rvest,
  tidyr
            )
```

## Get US measles
```{r read-data, echo=FALSE}
## read the data in a file online
file <- "https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/number-of-measles-cases.zip?v=1&csvType=filtered&useColumnShortNames=false&yScale=linear"
df_measles_US  <- import(file, which = 2, trust  = TRUE)
colnames(df_measles_US) <- c("country", "code", "year", "cases", "annotations")
```

## Check out the variables
```{r load data, include false}
# Setting the seed based on the current time
glimpse(df_measles_US)
```

## plot the US cases
```{r deaths, include false}
measles_plot <- ggplot(df_measles_US, aes(x = year, y = cases)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1) +
  #geom_point(color = "darkred", size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Measles cases in USA",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Cases"
  ) +
  scale_y_log10() +  # Add logarithmic y-axis
  theme_minimal()
ggplotly(measles_plot)
```

# Calculate deaths incidence
```{r incidence, include false}
# Multiply all columns in df_pop (except Year) by 1000
df_child <- df_child %>%
  mutate(across(-year, ~ .x * 1000000))

  # Join df_deaths and df_pop_scaled on Year
df_combined <- df_measles_US %>%
  inner_join(df_child, by = "year")  # keep only years in df_deaths

df_combined <- df_combined %>%
  mutate(cases_per_child = cases / children * 1000000)
```

## plot incidnce
```{r mean-deaths, include false}
mean_Killed_per_Total <- mean(df_combined$Killed_per_Total, na.rm = TRUE) 
sd_Killed_per_Total <- sd(df_combined$Killed_per_Total, na.rm = TRUE)
se_Killed_per_Total <- sd(df_combined$Killed_per_Total, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(df_combined$Killed_per_Total)))
ymin_Killed_per_Total <- mean_Killed_per_Total - sd_Killed_per_Total
ymax_Killed_per_Total <- mean_Killed_per_Total + sd_Killed_per_Total


# Minor grid lines
minor_vals <- unlist(
  lapply(-1:4, function(i) (1:9) * 10^i)
)

# Major ticks
major_vals <- 10^(-1:5)

# Exclude major tick positions
minor_vals <- minor_vals[!minor_vals %in% major_vals]

# Create plot
combined_plot <- plot_ly(
  data = df_combined,
  x = ~year,
  y = ~cases_per_child,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines",
  line = list(color = "steelblue", width = 4),
  hovertemplate = paste(
    "Year: %{x}<br>",
    "Cases per million children: %{y}<extra></extra>"
  )
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "Measles incidence USA",
    xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Cases per million children",
      type = "log",
      range = c(-1, 5),
      tickmode = "array",
      tickvals = major_vals,
      ticktext = c("10⁻¹", "10⁰", "10¹",
                  "10²", "10³", "10⁴", "10⁵"),
      showgrid = TRUE,
      minor = list(ticks = "", showgrid = FALSE),
      gridcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0.25)",    #major grid color
      gridwidth = 1                     #major grid size
    ),
    shapes = lapply(minor_vals, function(v) {
      list(
        type = "line",
        xref = "paper",
        x0 = 0, x1 = 1,
        yref = "y",
        y0 = v, y1 = v,
        line = list(
          color = "rgba(0,0,0,0.10)",
          width = 0.5
        ),
        layer = "below"
      )
    }),
    template = "plotly_white"
  )

# Display plot
combined_plot
```

## Get UK measles data
```{r mean-deaths, include false}
url <- "https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/measles-historic-confirmed-cases-notifications-and-deaths/measles-historic-confirmed-cases-notifications-and-deaths"
webpage <- read_html(url)

# Locate the target heading node
target_node <- webpage %>%
  html_element(xpath = "//h2[contains(text(), 'Measles notifications and deaths')] | //h3[contains(text(), 'Measles notifications and deaths')]")

# Extract and clean table dynamically
df_measles_UK <- target_node %>%
  html_element(xpath = "following-sibling::table[1]") %>%
  html_table() %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  # Select and rename the first 3 columns directly
  select(Year = 1, Cases = 2, Deaths = 3) %>%
  # Clean out footnotes/text in cells BEFORE parsing numbers
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ gsub("\\[.*?\\]|\\(.*\\)", "", .))) %>%
  # Extract numeric values (works even with trailing text like 'provisional')
  mutate(
    Year = as.integer(parse_number(Year)),
    Cases = as.numeric(parse_number(Cases)),
    Deaths = as.integer(parse_number(Deaths))
  ) %>%
  # Drop non-year/header/footer rows
  filter(!is.na(Year) & Year >= 1940)

# Check the last rows to confirm 2025 and 2026 are present
tail(df_measles_UK)
```

## plot UK measles
```{r deaths, include false}
plot_measles_UK <- ggplot(df_measles_UK, aes(x = Year, y = Cases)) +
  geom_line(color = "darkred", size = 1) +
  #geom_point(color = "darkred", size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Measles cases in UK",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Cases"
  ) +
  scale_y_log10() +  # Add logarithmic y-axis
  theme_minimal()
ggplotly(plot_measles_UK)
```

## Get the US child population data
## source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260218205227if_/https://www.childstats.gov/americaschildren/tables/xls/pop1.xlsx
```{r read-data, echo=FALSE}
file <- "pop1.xlsx"
df_temp <- import(file, trust = TRUE)

df1 <- df_temp[1:2, , drop = FALSE]  # rows 1 and 2, keep as data.frame
#df1 <- as.matrix(df1)  # remove column names
rownames(df1) <- NULL
colnames(df1) <- NULL
df1 <- t(df1)
df1 <- df1[-1, ]
df1 <- as.data.frame(df1)

df2 <- df_temp[8:9, , drop = FALSE]  # rows 8 and 8, keep as data.frame
#df2 <- as.matrix(df2)  # remove column names
rownames(df2) <- NULL
colnames(df2) <- NULL
df2 <- t(df2)
df2 <- df2[-1, ]
df2 <- as.data.frame(df2)

df3 <- df_temp[15:16, , drop = FALSE]  # rows 15 and 16, keep as data.frame
#df3 <- as.matrix(df3)  # remove column names
rownames(df3) <- NULL
colnames(df3) <- NULL
df3 <- t(df3)
df3 <- df3[-1, ]
df3 <- as.data.frame(df3)

df4 <- df_temp[22:23, , drop = FALSE]  # rows 22 and 23, keep as data.frame
#df4 <- as.matrix(df4)  # remove column names
rownames(df4) <- NULL
colnames(df4) <- NULL
df4 <- t(df4)
df4 <- df4[-1, ]
df4 <- as.data.frame(df4)

df_child <- bind_rows(df1, df2, df3, df4)
colnames(df_child) <- c("year", "children")
df_child$year <- as.numeric(df_child$year)
df_child$children <- as.numeric(df_child$children)
df_child <- head(df_child, -6)

glimpse(df_child)

# Add years
df_child <- df_child %>%
  add_row(year = 2024, children = 72.548879)
df_child <- df_child %>%
  add_row(year = 2025, children = 72.021348)
df_child <- df_child %>%
  add_row(year = 2026, children = 71.683186)


# Get projection for 2026
df_historical <- df_child %>% 
  filter(year >= 2021 & year <= 2025)
model <- lm(children ~ year, data = df_historical)
df_2026 <- data.frame(year = 2026)
projection_2026 <- predict(model, newdata = df_2026)


glimpse(df_child)
```
